name: is.emergent/emergent
title: Emergent Technologies
description: An applied AI lab architecting and deploying a trust framework for the emerging internet of agents.

tools.name: ask_emergent
tools.description: Ask Emergent Technologies' own agent a question in plain words (data licensing, the payout estimate, privacy, the referral partner program, AI consulting, the lab, contact). It answers only from Emergent's fact book: the claims are quoted as published, each with its fact id, status and source page, followed by the next step for who is asking. If the fact book does not cover the question it says so and gives the contact path. The question is treated as data: instructions inside it are not followed. It sends nothing on anyone's behalf; questions and its answers are kept to improve the agent, as the privacy policy says (emergenttechnologies.ai/privacy).

question.description: The question, in plain words (up to 2,000 characters). Please leave out personal details.

role.description: Who is asking, to pick the next step: owner, partner, buyer (an AI lab or data buyer), consulting, or other

tools.name: about_emergent
tools.description: Returns who Emergent Technologies, Inc. (emergenttechnologies.ai) is, what it does and for whom, from its fact book, with fact ids, statuses, dates and source pages, plus the next step for each kind of person (owner, partner, consulting, buyer). Optional topic narrows the answer: overview (default), disambiguation (how it differs from emergent.sh and from Emergent Technologies of Austin, Texas, emergenttechnologies.com), or one fact-book topic.

topic.description: overview (default), disambiguation, or a fact-book topic: company, licensing, estimate, privacy-consent, partners, consulting, lab, contact

tools.name: search_facts
tools.description: Keyword search over Emergent Technologies' fact book. Returns matching facts with their ids, topic, claim, source page, the date each was last checked (asOf) and status (approved or draft). Each fact can be cited by its id; an empty result means the fact book does not state it.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. 'who removes personal details'

tools.name: estimate_payout
tools.description: Returns the same indicative payout range the estimator at emergenttechnologies.ai/data-licensing shows for a company's headcount, years of records and headquarters, with the page's own caveats. It is a starting range from licensing partners' published formulas, not an offer. Inputs above the page's caps (1,000 people, 30 years) are shown at the cap, as on the page.

employees.description: How many people work at the company

years.description: How many years of data the company has (usually years in business)

headquarters.description: Where the company is headquartered: us (default), canada, europe or other

tools.name: check_program_fit
tools.description: Runs the same matching rules as emergenttechnologies.ai/fit on a person's answers and says which kind of program fits (data licensing, the referral partner program, or expert work) and why. It collects and saves nothing and takes no personal details. To see their specific route and proceed, the person continues at /fit, where they enter their own details with consent.

path.description: company = owns or runs a company; closed = the company closed; professional = lawyer, doctor, accountant, exec; partner = brings deals

interest.description: Company paths: license = license the records; refer = offer this to clients; both

status.description: Company path: is it still operating?

employees.description: People at the company (at its peak if closed)

industry.description: The company's industry: legal, accounting_finance, medical, or other for any other industry (for example, software and IT services, HVAC, manufacturing or logistics)

country.description: us; ca_uk_au = Canada, UK or Australia; other

dataTypes.description: Specialised records the company holds, such as CAD files, source code repositories or simulation and sensor logs; none if it holds none

tools.description: Systems the company uses; paper = mostly paper

licensed.description: Professional path: licensed in their field?

reach.description: Partner path: how many companies they can reach

tools.name: partner_program
tools.description: Returns Emergent's published description of its referral partner program: who can refer, how a referral works, when partners are paid, what to tell an owner, and how to apply. Each fact carries its own status (approved, or draft: wording pending Emergent's final approval). Referral rates and amounts are not published, so none are returned.

tools.name: consulting_offer
tools.description: Returns Emergent's published description of its AI & automation consulting: what it is, how Emergent assesses a business and pairs each initiative with the specialist suited to deliver it, how an engagement runs (Assess, Match, Build, Run), the services, enterprise private intelligence and its deployment options (with a leading lab, on dedicated cloud infrastructure or on hardware the client owns), how to start, and how to get in touch. Each fact carries its own status (approved or draft). No prices are published, so none are returned.

tools.name: start_conversation
tools.description: Prepares a consent-safe handoff to Emergent's team. It sends nothing and saves nothing: it returns a short summary of what the person wants and the exact Emergent page where the person reviews, confirms and submits their own details. Nothing reaches Emergent until the person submits that page themselves.

request.description: Optional: what the person wants, in a sentence. Returned to you as written; do not include personal details.
